message.content:
Copernicus was criticized by Aristotelian astronomers, Catholic authorities, and later astronomers who defended the Ptolemaic system.  
Tycho Brahe rejected the idea of a moving Earth, and Christoph Clavius argued that the Earth-centered model was more reliable.  
Many early scholars called his heliocentric theory implausible, though some also recognized its mathematical promise.  
Who were the critics of Nicolaus Copernicus?  
Did Tycho Brahe and Clavius challenge his model?  
Did Catholic authorities place restrictions on his work?  
What a bold challenge to ancient astronomy!  
How strange the moving Earth seemed to them!  
What a controversy it sparked!
